title: Ordinary least squares as a named criterion
dek: Wikipedia OLS is argmin of squared residuals. Geometry, Gauss–Markov, and sandwich SEs already have Simplfy plates.
story: Ordinary least squares on Wikipedia is a criterion: choose β to minimise ‖y − Xβ‖². It is not automatically a Gaussian likelihood, not automatically causal, and not automatically the BLUE unless Gauss–Markov assumptions hold.
stats-ols-geometry already draws the projection. stats-gauss-markov already states BLUE. stats-sandwich already handles heteroscedasticity. This card is the encyclopedia name of the criterion.
NIST's least-squares language is the definitional authority when Wikipedia and a lab notebook disagree about what was optimised.
deep: Under iid Gaussian errors, OLS = MLE. Without that, OLS is still a projection estimator with a sandwich variance.
Normal equations XᵀX β̂ = Xᵀy are linear algebra, not a DAG.
Do not call a logit fit 'OLS' because the software defaulted to a linear probability model.

visual.caption: OLS as a reduced criterion (squared residuals) sitting inside the fuller Gaussian-likelihood story. They coincide when errors are iid Normal; they part when they are not.
